text: Early one morning in April 1883, I woke up to find Sherlock Holmes standing by my bed, fully dressed. <break time="0.8s" /> A young lady has come to see us in a great hurry, and I thought you would want to hear her story from the beginning. <break time="0.8s" /> The lady was dressed in black and wore a heavy veil, and she was shaking like a frightened animal. <break time="0.8s" /> It is not the cold that makes me shake, Mister Holmes, she said in a low voice, It is fear. <break time="0.8s" /> When she lifted her veil, we saw that her face was pale and her hair was already touched with gray, though she was still young. <break time="0.8s" /> Her name was Helen Stoner, and she lived with her stepfather, Doctor Grimesby Roylott, in an old house at Stoke Moran. <break time="0.8s" /> Doctor Roylott was the last member of a family that had once been very rich, but it had lost almost everything long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> He had worked as a doctor in India, where his terrible temper had once caused the death of a servant and sent him to prison. <break time="0.8s" /> After Helens mother died in a railway accident, her money went to Doctor Roylott as long as her daughters lived with him. <break time="0.8s" /> Now he had no friends at all except the wandering gypsies, and he kept a cheetah and a baboon that ran freely around his land.
